title.narrative: Strengthening Community Protection and Tech-Enabled GBV/CP Services for Crisis-Affected Women, Children, and Persons with Disabilities in Madagali, Adamawa State

description.narrative: ltpgtThe protracted conflict in Adamawa State continues to expose women, children, and persons with disabilities in Madagali LGA to severe protection risks—including GBV, child labor, exploitation, family separation, and harmful coping mechanisms driven by displacement, insecurity, and limited access to essential services. With Madagali classified in CH Phase 3+, and gaps in existing child protection and GBV services, urgent, locally led protection interventions are required to safeguard dignity and strengthen community resilience.ltbrgtThis project aims to reduce protection risks and enhance access to survivor-centered services through a comprehensive, community-driven protection package. CATAI will establish one safe, inclusive Women and Girls Safe Space (WGSS) and two adolescent clubs that provide basic psychosocial support (PSS), life skills, structured GBV/CP awareness sessions, and confidential referrals. Trained caseworkers will deliver quality case management to 200 GBV survivors and 200 vulnerable children, ensuring safety planning, PFA, follow-up, and referrals to specialized services.ltbrgtTo prevent further harm, the project will strengthen community-based protection systems by revitalizing and supporting Community-Based Child Protection Committees (CBCPCs), women's groups, and adolescent peer networks. These structures will lead community risk mapping, early identification of vulnerable individuals, and safe referral to appropriate services. Caregivers of vulnerable children will receive targeted, protective livelihood support—limited to IGAs with direct protection outcomes—to reduce negative coping mechanisms such as early marriage and child labor.ltbrgtAn innovative digital protection reporting system will be deployed, utilizing USSD, WhatsApp Chatbot, and a toll-free hotline to enable safe, anonymous, multi-language reporting. This system expands access for low-literacy populations, hard-to-reach communities, and persons with disabilities, enhancing accountability, early warning, and confidential referrals.ltbrgtDisability inclusion is mainstreamed throughout the project. Facilities will be made physically accessible, IEC materials adapted for diverse needs, and a Disability Inclusion Focal Point will ensure meaningful participation. Collaboration with OPDs will strengthen referral pathways and ensure that persons with disabilities are fully represented in community structures. The project explicitly strengthens Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP) by ensuring that at least 80% of targeted individuals can access safe, confidential, and inclusive feedback and complaint mechanisms through community-based and digital channels..ltbrgtOverall, the project will provide life-saving, survivor-centered protection assistance to 8,150 individuals, strengthen local protection systems, expand safe reporting channels, and promote inclusive, community-led resilience in one of the most underserved LGAs in Adamawa State.lt/pgt
